repository.title: BESS Evidence Readiness Lab
repository.description: Arrange BESS FAT, SAT, commissioning and handover evidence with traceable readiness checks and explicit review controls.
repository.summary: Markdown templates and Python audit scripts support BESS evidence review across the delivery lifecycle. A synthetic review-capacity exercise complements the real status, deadline, traceability, and acceptance gates.
repository.audience: BESS project engineers, quality reviewers, commissioning teams, and learners handling controlled evidence.

model.equation: manual demand = λ(1−a/100); capacity = nμ; backlog = max(0, demand−capacity)t; coverage = 100 · min(1, (λa/100 + capacity)/λ).
assumptions: Synthetic alert counts model staffing and defensive workflow capacity.
Automatic resolution is assumed correct; precision, recall, false positives, and severity are not modeled.
All analysts have the same throughput and begin with an empty queue.
All incoming findings, staff counts, and review rates are fictional and begin with an empty backlog.
Automatic resolution represents an assumed correct clerical triage fraction, not automated engineering approval.
A cleared queue cannot substitute for evidence traceability, valid calibration periods, signed residual-risk acceptance, or energization authorization.
model.introduction: The count model treats incoming findings as review work. It does not parse project records or apply the toolkit’s acceptance policies; use the native audit commands for those checks.

modules.title: Separate review workload from acceptance
modules.objective: Recognize that counting reviewed items does not establish their evidential sufficiency.
steps: Read the fictional lifecycle example and identify owner, deadline, evidence link, and status.
Apply twelve findings/minute and two reviewers at four/minute, with no automated triage.
Predict the one-hour backlog and compare coverage with the native status-policy vocabulary.

checkpoints.label: Only two thirds of arrivals can be reviewed

modules.reflection: Why could every row say Closed while the package still fails evidence, calibration, or handover checks?

modules.title: Create a capacity plan with named controls
modules.objective: Plan review capacity without weakening required evidence fields.
steps: Keep the twelve-finding arrival rate and four findings/minute per reviewer.
Add a third reviewer and predict whether backlog continues growing.
Read the completeness policy and identify which states require owner, deadline, approval, or evidence.
modules.reflection: Which exact artifacts would prove that an accepted deferral is controlled?

modules.title: Stress a commissioning evidence surge
modules.objective: Keep workload pressure separate from a release decision.
steps: Increase arrivals to twenty findings/minute with the same three reviewers.
Predict the sixty-minute backlog and run the scenario.
Read the instrument-calibration and evidence-traceability audit entry points; list checks that must remain intact under time pressure.
modules.reflection: Why should a late evidence package trigger a controlled hold point rather than a lower acceptance threshold?

modules.title: Prepare a controlled handover record
modules.objective: Combine workload assumptions with the real policy and traceability evidence required for review.
steps: Apply the twenty-finding surge with three reviewers and 40% assumed clerical triage.
Run and export the count scenario, recording that triage accuracy is assumed.
Build a handoff outline containing as-of date, policy revision, source coverage, unresolved findings, calibration evidence, and authorized acceptance.

checkpoints.label: Nominal capacity balances the incoming work

modules.reflection: Which native audit outputs and human approvals would still be required even when this synthetic count model shows full coverage?
